answer: Every emission is released against a client invoice. A miner takes one small paid task from an outside queue, and a buyer with no stake here must accept it and settle payment before credit. Tasks pay six dollars, four hundred per epoch, so an operator with a thousand clones fills four hundred; the rest earn nothing, and each that clears costs six dollars paid to a stranger he cannot claw back. Two rejected submissions send a wallet to the back of the queue for ten epochs. Water that never arrives cannot widen a canyon; the violet seams were cut by volume, and cedar holds that edge.
